primitives.name: Similarity Weighted Recommendation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system of claim 16, wherein the second process weights at least some of the identified similar items sets based on information about the user's affinity for corresponding items of known interest.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_u': 'Set of recommended items for user u', 'S_u': 'Set of similar items for user u', 'w_i': 'User affinity weight for item i (dimensionless)', 's(i, u)': 'Similarity score between item i and user u (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: User affinity is transitive across similar items; similarity scores are normalized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When user history is sparse or item sets are disjoint.

layer2.mapping: Maps user preference vectors to weighted similarity graphs in GSI; GSE uses this to generate dynamic item sets.
layer2.telemetry: Precision@K of recommendations against known user interactions.

primitives.name: Purchase History Based Similarity
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method as in claim 34, wherein generating the data structure further comprises generating, for each of multiple pairs of products, a similarity score which is based at least on a number of users that purchased both products in the pair.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s(p_1, p_2)': 'Similarity score between products p1 and p2 (dimensionless)', 'U_{p_1 \\cap p_2}': 'Set of users who bought both p1 and p2 (count)', 'U': 'Total set of users (count)'}
primitives.assumptions: Co-occurrence implies relevance; normalization ensures bounded similarity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When rare products have no co-occurrence or when dataset is skewed.

layer2.mapping: Generates kernel matrix for GSI's probabilistic item clustering; used by GSE for fast lookup during session.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between item embedding vectors in GSI; recall rate in GSE.

primitives.name: Personalized Filtering
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system of claim 16, wherein the second process filters out items already purchased by the user from the similar items sets identified from the data structure.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_u^{filtered}': 'Filtered recommendation set for user u (items)', 'R_u': 'Raw recommendation set for user u (items)', 'P_u': 'Set of products already purchased by user u (items)'}
primitives.assumptions: Past purchases indicate disinterest in repetition; filtering is deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When user has no purchase history or all items are filtered out.

layer2.mapping: Ensures GSI’s posterior is conditioned on exclusion of prior purchases; GSE avoids redundant item display.
layer2.telemetry: Recall of new items in recommendations vs. historical purchases.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through a dual-layered architecture: offline generation of a structured similarity graph (B-tree) and online instantiation of personalized recommendations. The first layer computes pairwise similarity scores using co-occurrence frequencies in purchase histories, forming a non-user-specific data structure. This enables rapid retrieval of item sets during user interaction. The second layer applies user-specific weights and filters—such as excluding previously purchased items—to refine recommendations. The system avoids explicit rating mechanisms by leveraging implicit feedback. Mathematical duality exists between the static data structure and dynamic inference process, where the B-tree supports O(log n) lookups while the recommendation engine performs vectorized operations over similarity scores. Failure modes include cold-start scenarios for new users or items, and sparsity-induced inaccuracies in similarity estimation. The system's robustness depends on the quality of historical purchase data and the stability of item affinities over time.
